DESIGN REVIEW · FIT PENDING

KITTY, with her own signature.

A folded chest collar and faceted neck cuff give the compact Sentinel a shared design language. Two discreet rear cable-tie eyes and a tail-removal arrow make the details useful. The clipped phone bezel, curled detachable tail and your measured component sizes are retained.

Review the shape

The broad, bevelled chest V echoes the clipped ears and the faceted cuff on the shorter neck. Two rear tie eyes offer cable-tidying points without adding separate pieces. Their proposed 3.2 × 7 mm slots still need an actual tie/cable fit check. Aqua eyes are display placeholders matching the face app’s direction.

The tail uses a keyed socket and proposed M3 cross screw, above the service openings. Remove the screw, then follow the small arrow on the screw-entry side and pull rearward. The arrow shows direction only. Tail joint shows a 35 mm exploded gap; the screw is omitted. The proposed 0.4 mm fit clearance still needs a sample.

Before creating the final print set

The draft uses your 62 mm wheel diameter and 61 × 20 mm motor length/width. We still need motor height and shaft position, wheel hub fit, caster, AA holder, phone case/camera access, and printer bed/material/nozzle.

Each part needs fit and slicer/support review. The complete robot includes visual stand-ins for bought components; it is not a single object to print. Design approval and physical fit approval are separate steps.
